definition: A subjective test is an evaluation based on people’s judgments or perceptions rather than only on a mathematical or computer-based measure. In this context, it was used to compare results when two analysis methods gave different conclusions.

reasons: The packet does not define what a “subjective test” is in terms of “people’s judgments or perceptions.”
The packet does not support the claim that a subjective test is used “rather than only on a mathematical or computer-based measure.”

While the packet says the authors “performed a subjective test” to compare PCA vs SPCA and that it indicated SPCA was superior, it does not explicitly describe the subjective test’s basis or its contrast with mathematical/computer-based measures.

The definition generalizes “subjective test” as any evaluation based on people’s judgments or perceptions, but the packet only supports a specific use of a subjective test to compare inconsistent results between PCA and SPCA in this article.
The wording about a mathematical or computer-based measure is not stated in the packet and adds unsupported contrast beyond the source text.
